correctness.rationale: The self-adjoint point-interaction Schrödinger operator on circumference 2π has free-arc transfer P(k) and jump J(q), with det=1 and tr[J(β)P(k)J(α)P(k)]/2=cos(2πk)+((α+β)/(2k))sin(2πk)+(αβ/(2k²))sin²(πk). At half flux cos θ=−1 this factorizes into (R(k)+α)(R(k)+β)=0, R(k)=2k cot(πk), strictly decreasing from 0 to −∞ on each (n+1/2,n+1); positive barriers yield one k_n(q) per interval and no other levels. For equal q the one-arc matrix has trace 0 and determinant 1, hence its square is −I and geometric multiplicity exactly two; unequal strengths give distinct simple levels. Implicit differentiation gives dE_n/dq=2k_n/D_n(q) with D_n=2πk_n+q/k_n+πq²/(2k_n), so 0<dE_n/dq<1/π; integration yields a sharp energy-splitting upper bound |α−β|/π approached as n→∞. Expanding the exact squared relation (R+g)²=d²+[2k cos(θ/2)/sinπk]² near (k_n(g),g,g,π) gives gap (4k_n/D_n)√(d²+(k_n²+g²/4)ε²)+O(d²+ε²); nonuniformity in n is acknowledged. Independently multiplied transfer matrices, finite root brackets and coupling derivatives agreed. Numerical tests are corroboration, not the infinite-level proof.
